assumptions: The service does not take title to or possession of salvaged inventory, and specialist surveys, testing, removal, transport, storage, and regulated waste handling remain contracted or passed through as stated.
Target customers control recurring pipelines containing enough substantial projects to permit screening before procurement, deinstallation, or waste classification closes the reuse option.
The licensed-operator-of-record arrangement can be implemented lawfully, while the service still obtains lot-specific advice on its own BDO, product-status, and liability obligations.
The stated prices, margin targets, and founder-net-worth sensitivity are hypotheses rather than evidence of demand or achieved economics.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid annual or recurring pilots with multiple Polish portfolio owners or demolition contractors; results from at least twenty representative sites showing screening cost, gate-pass rate, recoverable value, removal and specialist cost, time-to-sale, cancellation rate, and contribution margin; repeatable buyer demand within economical transport distance; renewal evidence; and written legal and insurer acceptance of the exact product, waste, title, warranty, and operator-of-record flows.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Screening a recurring project pipeline before paying for a full audit directly addresses the documented risk that audit and recovery costs overwhelm salvage value. Restricting the initial wedge to pre-sellable non-structural components and keeping waste handling with a licensed operator makes the insight materially sharper, although it is an execution refinement in a category already served by a close full-stack competitor.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Owners and demolition contractors face real separation, classification, scheduling, disposal, and potential recovery-value problems. However, audits are not generally mandated, small-site economics can be adverse, and no evidence establishes that Polish customers will pay a recurring screening retainer or a later audit fee; this is material uncertainty rather than proof of no demand.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: A retainer can fund early triage, the gate can prevent uneconomic full audits, and pass-through field costs limit capital exposure. Against that, retainer price, screening cost, pass rate, sale conversion, contribution margin, retention, CAC, and payback are all unknown; low reported marketplace order value and free or no-commission substitutes are direct evidence that transaction fees alone are fragile. Scalable owner earnings are not yet demonstrated.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Polish commercial portfolio owners and demolition contractors with recurring substantial projects form a coherent, reachable beachhead with a clear trigger. The economic size of the subset that has suitable non-structural lots, early access, and sufficient nearby buyer liquidity is unknown, so the beachhead may be much narrower than construction-and-demolition waste volumes imply.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Owning the recurring portfolio review could create an advantageous early control point and local Polish specialization may help. But Concular already offers the audit, digital inventory, marketplace, logistics, and insured or warranted installation stack, while other marketplaces lower transaction-price expectations. No exclusive supply, buyer channel, or regulatory position is evidenced.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A successful non-structural wedge could extend across component classes, additional owner portfolios, regions, compliance workflows, procurement, and decision software, with the paired outcome dataset improving later screening. Expansion into structural products or regulated material, however, adds testing, insurance, conformity, and waste-law complexity rather than becoming automatically easy.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Longitudinal site, gate, buyer-acceptance, yield, timing, and outcome data could compound into better triage and quoting, and portfolio relationships can create workflow stickiness. The service and dataset are initially replicable, the incumbent has comparable capabilities, and a planned EU audit-data platform may commoditize inventory information, so durability depends on transaction outcomes and contracted access that are not yet established.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: The gate offers a plausible cost and convenience advantage over commissioning full audits indiscriminately, and the operator-of-record design may simplify delivery for customers. There is no measured improvement in net recovery, time, risk, or total cost versus incumbents, conventional demolition contractors, or free marketplaces, so the advantage is credible but not yet strong enough to predict behavior change.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Poland's 2025 separation duties and broader EU circular-construction policy create attention and inventory pressure, while possible digital pre-demolition infrastructure could expand available supply. The guidance is non-binding, a general paid-audit mandate is absent, and public infrastructure could also commoditize the proposed data layer, making timing favorable but ambiguous.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Concentrating on a few recurring portfolio owners, demolition contractors, property managers, architects, and licensed waste operators is more plausible than building an open marketplace and is compatible with a relationship-light founder model after initial sales. There is no evidence of access, sales-cycle length, partner incentives, CAC, renewals, or sufficient two-sided buyer liquidity, and enterprise trust plus early site access may make acquisition slow.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder's data and AI skills fit screening and evidence reconciliation, a pilot appears possible within the stated capital and part-time limits, and specialists can perform field and regulated work. Nevertheless, lot-specific legal classification, hazardous materials, insurance, title, removal damage, demolition deadlines, and multi-party coordination remain substantial; scaling would require an operating team and delegation quality that have not been demonstrated.

highest_value_structural_change: Turn the offer into a closed, contract-backed recovery network: require an annual minimum-volume portfolio commitment from each supply-side customer and pre-commit repeat buyers or offtakers for one or two standardized non-structural component classes before a site can pass the gate. This would replace speculative marketplace liquidity with contracted throughput and make the outcome dataset more proprietary.
main_structural_strength: The recurring portfolio control point enables a low-cost screen before irreversible demolition decisions, so expensive specialist work is reserved for sites with a plausible net-value surplus.
primary_score_limiter: The model lacks evidence that customers will pay and renew a screening retainer or that enough sites can clear the gate and produce repeatable contribution margin after buyer acquisition, specialist work, removal, transport, and coordination.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Concular already integrates essentially the proposed audit-to-inventory-to-marketplace-to-logistics workflow, while free or no-commission alternatives and RAEDIFICARE's roughly EUR 714 reported average order value directly undermine both differentiation and percentage-fee economics.
